title: Retrieved context versus the model's own knowledge

asked.text: In ClashEval, how does the calibrated token-probability method decide between the document and the model's own answer, and how much does it help? A short answer is fine.

report:
[Wu et al. 2024](owlit://library/arxiv-2404.10198) compare the answer's mean token probability with and without the document and keep the more confident one; calibrated, this raises accuracy by 14% and improves context bias by 20%. It is a remedy for one direction of the conflict: a model following a wrong document.

The other three papers frame that conflict. [Sun et al. 2024](owlit://library/arxiv-2410.11414) study the opposite failure, a model overriding a correct document with what it already holds. [Mallen et al. 2022](owlit://library/arxiv-2212.10511) give a reason the two meet: a model knows popular facts well and rare ones poorly, so which source should win depends on the fact. [Asai et al. 2023](owlit://library/arxiv-2310.11511) avoid part of the conflict by retrieving only when the model decides it needs to.

## What it means for your related work

Your paragraph cites ClashEval for models taking a wrong document over a correct prior; its token-probability correction is the one measured remedy here, and it addresses only that direction. A sentence on ReDeEP's opposite case would make the paragraph two-sided. What Mallen et al. and Self-RAG say here rests on their abstracts.

## Read first

[Wu et al. 2024](owlit://library/arxiv-2404.10198), for the method and its numbers; [Mallen et al. 2022](owlit://library/arxiv-2212.10511), for why the answer depends on the fact.
